newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TO SIGN TREATY WITH UKRAINE IN JUNE.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TO SIGN TREATY WITH UKRAINE IN JUNE.

text.p: Romania will sign a long-delayed key treaty with neighbouring Ukraine on June 2, expected to boost the Balkan country's chances to get an early admission in NATO, the foreign ministry said on Wednesday.
Romanian President Emil Constantinescu and his Ukrainian counterpart Leonid Kuchma will sign the treaty in the Black Sea port city of Constanta, a ministry statement said.
Bucharest has pressed with negotiating and signing the treaty after it has been told that Romania needs the pact with Ukraine to keep alive its chances of winning quick entry to NATO.

The statement said the treaty -- which proclaims the present borders as "inviolable" -- will be accompanied by an accord on steps to solve remaining differences, mainly in drawing the maritime borders in the Black Sea.
The treaty was initialled earlier this month in Kiev by the foreign ministers of the two countries, who had agreed to include differences in a separate accord.
The additional accord also settles that the two sides will turn to the International Court of Justice in the Hague if they fail to come to terms on the demarcation of the sea shelf.

After years of negotiations, Romania has dropped its insistence that Ukraine atone for the seizure by the Kremlin of large chunks of territory under the Nazi-Soviet pact which carved up eastern Europe. It has also abandoned a claim to a small Black Sea Island.
Romania won praise from Western leaders for signing a pact with Hungary last year, settling old rifts over borders and minorities.

The country's new centrist leaders hope that a similar deal with Ukraine will boost Romania's chances of being invited to join, along with favourited Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, when the Alliance announces its first eastward expansion at a Madrid summit in July.
